subject: spec.md
checked: All 16 acceptance criteria in spec.md read end to end, each for a given/when/then a single test could execute and a mechanically comparable expect
AC-001 against the ticket's 'Fresh install — no plaintext Monobank keys: migration performs zero writes' edge case
AC-002 and AC-003 against 'the migration copies monobank_personal_token and monobank_client_name ... into the encrypted store' — one key per criterion, not bundled
AC-004 and AC-005 against 'moves the existing values across and deletes the plaintext originals' — one deleted key per criterion
AC-006 against 'the plaintext copy is deleted only after the encrypted write is read back' — the shared call log makes the ordering a single assertable string comparison

AC-007 against 'Corrupted read-back — a non-null but non-equal read does not trigger the plaintext delete'; the given supplies a one-character-different read-back so the assertion can only pass by the gate existing
AC-008 and AC-009 against 'Value in both stores — encrypted wins, plaintext copy deleted, encrypted never overwritten' — split into the no-overwrite half and the delete half
AC-010 and AC-011 against 'One key succeeds, one fails — handled independently' — split into the migrated key's delete and the failed key's retained plaintext value
AC-012 against 'A failed migration is not fatal' — resolving undefined rather than rejecting is the testable half; the startup-path half is filed as VG-004, not asserted

AC-013 and AC-014 against 'Migration re-run — idempotent, detected per storage key by the plaintext key being absent'; AC-014's expected count of 2 is consistent with two keys migrating on run one and none on run two
AC-015 against 'Nothing else in plaintext MMKV is touched' — pins monobank_selected_account_ids, with the residual scope limit recorded as VG-007 rather than claimed
AC-016 against the ticket's docs surface, 'src/services/monobank/CLAUDE.md updated to describe the one-time migration'

Every surface listed in the ticket's 'Surfaces the change is seen through' section against the spec's surfaces field and the criteria carrying each: migration entry point (AC-012), plaintext MMKV (AC-004..AC-011, AC-015), encrypted SecretStore (AC-001..AC-003, AC-008, AC-013, AC-014), docs (AC-016)

AS-001 through AS-016 read one by one for content that is really a limit of verification rather than a statement of behaviour; each states how the system behaves, and the corresponding 'a green suite would not prove this' clauses are filed separately as VG-001 through VG-007

AS-006 (encrypted-wins deletes plaintext without a read-back) checked against the ticket's 'deleted only after the encrypted write is read back' rule — the ticket's rule is conditioned on a write having been issued, and the encrypted-wins branch issues none, so the spec records the decision rather than contradicting the ticket

VG-001 through VG-007 checked for being verification limits and not smuggled behaviour: in-memory doubles, real upgrade path, process-kill durability, startup wiring, the AS-011 race, log/crash-report leakage of AS-009, and the unpinned remainder of AS-002
The spec's non_goals against the ticket for anything the ticket asks for that the spec excludes — no overlap found
